messages:
emma_cs: FYI support escalation from Acme — their batch rerank results are returning scores that don't map to the per-query candidate lists. Impacting ranking for 3% of requests, customer marking P1. Trace: trace-9f3b.

raj_engineer: can you paste a sanitized request body and the response (or trace)? do we have a repro?

emma_cs: attaching a redacted payload and the server response we got. Note the customer sends 2 queries with per-query candidate lists.

emma_cs: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"queries": ["best italian restaurants near me","sushi delivery open now"],"candidate_lists": [["ristorante-a","trattoria-b"],["sushi-x","sushi-y","sushi-z"]],"top_k": 3}'

# server response (redacted):
{"scores": [0.9, 0.1, 0.7, 0.4, 0.6, 0.2], "candidates_flat": ["ristorante-a","trattoria-b","sushi-x","sushi-y","sushi-z","extra"], "note": "scores length == candidates_flat length"}
```

oncall_bot: [alert] rerank-response-mismatch detected for trace-9f3b — response_length_mismatch (rule rerank_length_check) :fire:

raj_engineer: thanks. quick read — the response flattened candidates and the mapping back to per-query buckets is wrong: customer expected first 2 scores for query1, next 3 for query2. but our scores appear shifted: the ordering looks like a global flatten and then a reorder that drops offsets when candidate_lists have unequal lengths. i'll try to reproduce locally.

raj_engineer: repro snippet i used: ```python
payload = {
  "queries": ["q1","q2"],
  "candidate_lists": [["a","b"],["c"]]
}
# call rerank, inspect response['scores'] and response['candidates_flat']
# observed mapping: scores assigned in round-robin instead of contiguous buckets
```

liam_infra: looking at logs around trace-9f3b — function reorderCandidatesByQuery computed start indices with a cumulative sum loop, but we found an off-by-one when candidate_lists had length >1 and we also applied a flatten+dedupe pass. excerpt:

```
INFO 2024-06-13T12:02:34Z reorderCandidatesByQuery startIdxs=[0,2] flat_len=5 computed_map=[0,2,4] // mismatch
WARN 2024-06-13T12:02:34Z dedupeFlatten applied -> removed placeholder at idx=4
```
liam_infra: seems the dedupe/placeholder logic runs after we compute offsets, so computed offsets point to wrong indices.

emma_cs: Customer asks for a temporary workaround until a fix is shipped. They can't batch per customer request volume.

raj_engineer: short-term workarounds:
- avoid sending multiple queries in a single request (split into separate rerank calls)
- or ensure each per-query candidate_list has the same length by padding with a distinct sentinel (e.g., "__NULL__") and then ignore sentinel results client-side
I know neither is great — i'll put a patch up.

sophie_support: Can we give Acme an ETA and a way to verify when fixed? they asked for a regression test and a patch window.

raj_engineer: i reproduced locally and wrote a unit test. root cause: offsets calc + post-flatten dedupe ordering. i'll push PR with fix + test. targeting staging deploy in ~2 hours, prod within 6 hours after verification.

emma_cs: sharing sanitized trace and sample payload with eng: trace-9f3b, sample above. customer confirmed they can accept split-requests workaround for next 6 hours if fix ETA holds.

zane_research: suggested test case added to our rerank suite: multiquery-varying-lengths -> assert contiguous score buckets per query. also added fuzzing to catch flatten+dedupe ordering cases.

raj_engineer: Patch merged to staging (PR #4821). Can someone from support run this curl against staging to verify mapping is restored? staging URL: https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank (use sandbox key).

emma_cs: i ran the staging request with Acme's sanitized payload; mapping looks correct now — first 2 scores belong to query1, next 3 to query2. forwarding to customer. :thumbsup:

raj_engineer: thanks — rolling to prod in ~4h after monitoring window. reopening ticket if anything else pops. leaving links to logs and PR in the internal ticket.

sophie_support: noted — sending patch ETA and workaround instructions to Acme. closing escalation loop once prod is live.

raj_engineer: follow-up action items: add end-to-end test in CI for multiquery flattening, add an invariant check in production that compares declared per-query counts against computed bucket boundaries and raises an alert if mismatch (helps auto-detect regressions).

emma_cs: thanks team — will update the customer now and mark as "monitoring" until prod deploy.
